status: selected regional evidence review; not a complete transcription of the skeleton layer
policy: The author authorizes representative use of sparse marsh and low-lane levels across the marsh regions established in the book. Retain surface role and date; these are proxies for field interiors. Later surface-specific evidence may raise developed ground. No modern fill is used to define historical marsh relief.

bookEvidence.path: West Ham and the River Lea_ A Social and E - Jim Clifford.pdf
bookEvidence.note: Map 2 (1805) and Marshlands and Early Industry establish broad marsh extent; book describes continued open marsh and development on former marsh. They do not establish point heights or exact model boundaries.

regions.description: Footpaths and Temple Mill/Homerton roads across Hackney Marsh, away from the river-bank path and bridge crest. Low-road proxy for regional marsh; no blanket fill subtraction.
Marsh Lane low end distinguished from its rise toward Church Lane and the Leyton terrace.
Low path across southern Hackney/Stratford marsh or Marsh Gate Lane margin, distinct from the reservoir and river embankments.
Minor dead-end lane east of Waterworks River and north of the railway; low lane surface used as a marsh proxy.
Abbey Mill Lane along northern Mill Meads; lane figures around 8 ft are distinct from 15–16 ft Three Mills Wall River banks.
Low lane/path on West Ham Abbey Marsh east of Abbey Creek, beside but distinct from the North Woolwich railway.
Star Lane/Forty Acres Lane on the low Plaistow marsh; ordinary lane surface, not the higher Barking Road or a benchmark.
Green Lane/Dirty Lane/Prince Regent Lane across Plaistow Marsh; low lanes used as representative ground proxies.
Southern Green Lane across Plaistow Marsh before dock construction; not a Thames flood-wall crest.

limitations: Most accepted values measure low lanes or margins, not surveyed field interiors. No uniform 30 cm accuracy is established.
Datum and map registration remain provisional; no independent calibration has been performed.
Benchmarks, riverbanks, crossings and major raised roads are retained as comparisons, excluded from the underlying marsh surface.
The blank interiors are a lack of levelling marks, not evidence for modern terrain.
Source epoch remains 1848–51; the working 1900 substrate uses the author’s continuity assumption.
